subject: agriculture
topicTitle: Fruits and Vegetables Production, Floriculture, Post-Harvest Management, Landscaping
thirtySecondSummary: Horticulture encompasses Pomology (fruits), Olericulture (vegetables), Floriculture (flowers & ornamental plants), Post-Harvest Management, and Landscaping.

Asexual propagation methods preserve true-to-type elite clones: Air layering / Gootee (Litchi, Guava), T-budding / Shield budding (Rose, Citrus), Inarching & Veneer grafting (Mango), and Stooling / Mound layering (Guava).

Major fruit crops possess specialized agro-climatic demands: Mango (Alphonso, Dashehari, Amrapali: dwarf hybrid suited for high-density planting at 2.5 x 2.5 m), Banana (Grand Naine, Cavendish, propagated via sword suckers), Papaya (dioecious/gynodioecious, papain enzyme), and Citrus.

Post-harvest physiology categorizes fruits into Climacteric (ripen post-harvest with an ethylene and respiratory burst; e.g., Mango, Banana, Papaya, Guava) and Non-Climacteric (do not ripen after harvest; e.g., Citrus, Grape, Litchi, Pomegranate).

Food preservation standards mandate TSS (Total Soluble Solids) and fruit content: Jam (minimum 68% TSS, 45% fruit pulp), Jelly (minimum 65% TSS, 45% clear fruit juice, requires high pectin & acid; alcohol/sheet test), and Marmalade (citrus peel shreds).

coreConcepts.title: Asexual Plant Propagation Techniques in Fruit Crops
coreConcepts.explanation:
Vegetative propagation ensures genetic uniformity, earlier bearing, and dwarfing.
1. Cuttings: Stem cuttings (Hardwood: Grape, Pomegranate; Semi-hardwood: Guava; Softwood: Tea), Root cuttings (Blackberry), Leaf cuttings (Bryophyllum, Sansevieria). Auxin IBA (Indole-3-Butyric Acid) is applied to stimulate rooting.
2. Layering: Rooting induced while the stem remains attached to parent plant.
- Air Layering (Gootee): A 2.5 cm bark ring is removed from a 1-year-old shoot, treated with IBA (5000 ppm), wrapped in moist sphagnum moss, and enclosed in polythene (standard commercial method in Litchi).
- Stooling / Mound Layering: Mother plant headed back to ground level, shoots mounded with soil (commercial propagation of Guava and Apple rootstocks).
3. Grafting & Budding:
- Veneer & Epicotyl / Stone Grafting: Mango (Epicotyl grafting uses 8-15 day old germinating mango stones).
- T-Budding (Shield Budding): Rose, Citrus, Ber (an active scion bud slipped into a T-shaped incision on rootstock).
keyTakeaways: Air Layering (Gootee): Standard propagation for Litchi.
Epicotyl / Stone Grafting: Fast commercial propagation for Mango.
T-Budding (Shield Budding): Standard for Rose and Citrus.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit IV, Plant Propagation section, pp. 147-158.

coreConcepts.title: Production Technology of Major Fruit and Vegetable Crops
coreConcepts.explanation:
1. Mango (Mangifera indica): King of Fruits, National Fruit of India.
- Amrapali: Hybrid (Dashehari x Neelum); distinctly dwarf, highly precocious, regular bearer; ideal for high-density planting (HDP) at 2.5 x 2.5 m accommodating 1600 plants/ha.
- Mallika: (Neelum x Dashehari); highest Vitamin A content.
- Disorders: Malformation (Fusarium / hormonal imbalance), Black tip (caused by SO2 and carbon monoxide gases from brick kilns near orchards; prevented by spraying 1% Borax), Spongy tissue (internal breakdown in Alphonso caused by convective heat).
2. Banana (Musa paradisiaca): Heavy feeder, propagated by Sword Suckers weighing 500-750 g or tissue culture; commercial cultivar Grand Naine (AAA triploid).
3. Papaya (Carica papaya): Rich source of Vitamin A and proteolytic enzyme Papain; Gynodioecious varieties (Pusa Delicious, Pusa Majesty, Solo) yield 100% productive female and hermaphrodite trees without requiring separate male pollinizer trees.
4. Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum): Lycopene is the red pigment (maximum synthesis at 21-24°C; inhibited above 30°C); Blossom End Rot caused by Calcium (Ca) deficiency.
keyTakeaways: Amrapali Mango: Dwarf, suitable for High Density Planting (2.5 x 2.5 m, 1600 plants/ha).
Black Tip of Mango: Caused by brick kiln fumes (SO2, CO); sprayed with 1% Borax.
Papaya: Gynodioecious varieties yield only female and bisexual fruitful trees.
Lycopene synthesis in tomato: Optimum at 21-24°C; stops above 30°C.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit IV, Fruit & Vegetable Crops, pp. 160-174.

coreConcepts.title: Post-Harvest Management, Fruit Preservation and Landscaping
coreConcepts.explanation:
Post-harvest losses in fruits and vegetables in India reach 20-30% due to perishable biological nature.
1. Climacteric vs Non-Climacteric Fruits:
- Climacteric: Marked rise in respiration and burst of ethylene (C2H4) production during ripening; fruits can be harvested mature-green and ripened artificially (Mango, Banana, Papaya, Guava, Apple, Tomato).
- Non-Climacteric: No post-harvest respiratory or ethylene surge; must ripen fully on the plant before harvest (Citrus, Grape, Litchi, Pomegranate, Pineapple).
2. Preservation Standards (FSSAI / FPO):
- Jam: Minimum 68° Brix TSS, 45% fruit pulp (tested with refractometer).
- Jelly: Minimum 65° Brix TSS, 45% clear pectin-rich fruit extract. Pectin is essential (Guava, Sour Apple); tested by Alcohol test (clump formation) or Jelmeter. Sheet/Flake test confirms jelly endpoint at 105°C (221°F).
- Marmalade: Citrus fruit jelly incorporating suspended shreds of citrus peel.
- Chemical Preservatives: Sodium Benzoate (used for naturally colored products like tomato ketchup, berry juices; active as benzoic acid) vs Potassium Metabisulfite (KMS, releases SO2; used for colorless/light juices; bleached anthocyanin red pigments, so never used for red jams).
3. Principles of Landscaping: Formal (symmetrical, Mughal gardens like Shalimar / Taj Mahal) vs Informal (asymmetrical, Japanese gardens, English landscape gardens with natural flowing curves, lawns, and rockeries).
keyTakeaways: Climacteric (Mango, Banana, Apple) vs Non-climacteric (Citrus, Grape, Litchi).
Jam standard: 68° Brix TSS; Jelly standard: 65° Brix TSS (endpoint 105°C).
KMS preservative: Releases SO2, prohibited in colored products due to bleaching.
Sodium Benzoate: Preservative for colored fruit products (tomato sauce, ketchup).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: ICAR Class XII Unit IV, Post-Harvest & Landscaping, pp. 176-187.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Spacing: 2.5 m x 2.5 m = 1600 plants per hectare
keyFacts.explanation: Developed at IARI New Delhi; dwarf hybrid allows ultra-high density compared to traditional 10 x 10 m spacing (100 plants/ha).
keyFacts.examTip: CUET frequently tests the spacing and parentage (Dashehari x Neelum) of Amrapali.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: TSS 65° Brix | Boiling Temperature: 105°C (221°F) | Sheet / Flake Test
keyFacts.explanation: When dropped from a cold spoon, the boiling jelly forms a wide sheet rather than flowing as separate drops.
keyFacts.examTip: Guava is the most ideal fruit for jelly making due to naturally rich pectin and acid.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Etiology: Brick kiln fumes (SO2, CO, Ethylene) | Control: 1% Borax spray
keyFacts.explanation: Necrosis of the fruit apex turning brownish-black, causing premature drop.
keyFacts.examTip: Orchards should not be located within 1.5 to 2 km of operating brick kilns.

keyFacts.explanation: Potent antimicrobial agent against yeast, molds, and bacteria; must never be used in dark/red-colored juices because SO2 bleaches anthocyanin pigments.
keyFacts.examTip: Sodium Benzoate is preferred for red-colored products.

workedExamples.question: Which of the following fruits is strictly classified as a 'Non-Climacteric' fruit that does NOT exhibit a post-harvest respiratory or ethylene surge and must ripen fully on the tree before harvest?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Understand climacteric vs non-climacteric fruits.
Step 2: Climacteric fruits (Mango, Banana, Papaya, Guava, Apple) can be harvested at physiological maturity and ripen post-harvest accompanied by an ethylene burst.
Step 3: Citrus fruits (Sweet Orange, Mandarin, Lime) alongside Grapes and Pomegranates are non-climacteric and will not ripen or sweeten once detached from the mother tree.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Climacteric vs non-climacteric fruit sorting is a very regular question in CUET Section II Agriculture.

workedExamples.question: What is the statutory minimum Total Soluble Solids (TSS in °Brix) required for commercial 'Fruit Jam' under Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regulations?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Recall statutory TSS standards: Fruit Jam requires minimum 68% TSS (68° Brix).
Step 2: (Fruit Jelly requires minimum 65% TSS / 65° Brix).
Step 3: Both products require a minimum of 45% fruit pulp/juice content.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Black tip disorder in mango is caused by which factor?
howCuetAsks.strategy: Identify sulfur dioxide (SO2) and carbon monoxide fumes emitting from nearby brick kilns, remedied by 1% Borax spray.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Match Litchi, Rose, Mango, and Banana with Air Layering, T-Budding, Epicotyl Grafting, and Sword Suckers.
howCuetAsks.strategy: Anchor your match on Litchi = Air Layering (Gootee) and Rose = T-Budding.

commonTraps.trap: Using Potassium Metabisulfite (KMS) for red-colored fruit juices.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: KMS releases SO2 gas which permanently bleaches anthocyanin red pigments, turning red syrups and ketchups dull white.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Use Sodium Benzoate for naturally colored red/purple products.

commonTraps.trap: Confusing Amrapali and Mallika mango traits.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: Amrapali is Dashehari x Neelum (dwarf, high density); Mallika is Neelum x Dashehari (highest Vitamin A).
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Amrapali = D x N (Dwarf); Mallika = N x D (Nutritious/Vit A).

mnemonics.meaning: Jam requires 68° Brix TSS (while Jelly is 65° Brix).

practiceQuestions.question: Which plant growth regulator is universally used as a commercial rooting hormone for treating stem cuttings and air layers?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Indole-3-Butyric Acid (IBA), a synthetic auxin, is the most widely adopted rooting stimulant in vegetative propagation.

practiceQuestions.question: The dwarf mango hybrid 'Amrapali' developed by IARI New Delhi was obtained from which parental cross?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Amrapali is a cross between Dashehari (female) and Neelum (male) [D x N], yielding dwarf trees suitable for high density planting.

practiceQuestions.question: Why is Potassium Metabisulfite (KMS) strictly avoided as a chemical preservative in tomato sauce, red jam, and pomegranate juice?

options.text: It is highly toxic to human health
The sulfur dioxide (SO2) gas released bleaches natural red anthocyanin pigments
It increases acidity above legal limits

practiceQuestions.explanation: KMS releases SO2 which acts as a powerful reducing and bleaching agent, decolorizing natural red anthocyanin pigments.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): Guava is considered the most ideal fruit for commercial jelly preparation.
Reason (R): Slightly under-ripe guava fruits possess high natural concentrations of both pectin and acid, which are vital for establishing a firm pectin-sugar-acid gel network.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both statements are completely true and (R) provides the exact biochemical justification for why guava produces premier quality jelly.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Fruit Crop) with List-II (Standard Commercial Propagation Method):
List-I:
(P) Litchi
(Q) Rose
(R) Banana
(S) Mango

List-II:
(1) Sword Suckers
(2) Air Layering (Gootee)
(3) T-Budding (Shield)
(4) Epicotyl / Stone Grafting
practiceQuestions.explanation: Litchi = Air Layering; Rose = T-Budding; Banana = Sword Suckers; Mango = Epicotyl Grafting.

practiceQuestions.question: The boiling temperature indicating the successful completion/end-point of fruit jelly preparation is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: When fruit jelly reaches a TSS of 65° Brix, the boiling temperature reaches exactly 105°C (221°F) at sea level, signaling the completion of cooking.

practiceQuestions.question: Which physiological disorder in mango is caused by fumes of sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide released from brick kilns located in the vicinity of orchards?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Black tip disorder of mango is triggered by sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide fumes from nearby operational brick kilns, managed by spraying 1% Borax.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following is an informal, asymmetrical style of gardening that mimics raw natural countryside landscapes with flowing streams and rockeries?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Japanese and English landscape gardens follow the informal style of landscape architecture characterized by asymmetry, natural contours, and organic forms.

practiceQuestions.question: The red color in ripe tomatoes is imparted by which carotenoid pigment, whose synthesis is optimal at 21-24°C?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Lycopene is the carotenoid pigment responsible for the vibrant red color of ripe tomatoes; its synthesis stops when temperatures exceed 30°C.

practiceQuestions.question: Papaya varieties termed 'Gynodioecious' produce which types of plants in the orchard?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Gynodioecious papaya varieties (e.g., Pusa Delicious, Solo) produce only female and bisexual trees, ensuring that 100% of the plants bear fruit.
